LESSON: HANDLING WASTE MATERIALS

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: PRE-TECHNICAL STUDIES
Strand: Materials for Production
Topic 3.2: Handling Waste Materials
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 8

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Handling Waste Materials, part of Materials for Production in Grade 9 PRE-TECHNICAL STUDIES.

Key inquiry question: How are waste materials handled in the locality?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. walk around the school compound to identify waste materials, (plastic, glass, metal, wood waste, electronic waste, construction waste),

2. use print or digital media to search for information on safe ways of handling waste materials,

3. discuss safe ways of handling waste materials (reduce, reuse, recycle, compost and burn),

4. practise safe disposal of waste materials (reduce, reuse, recycle, compost and burn),

5. visit the locality to observe handling of waste materials.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. walk around the school compound to identify waste materials, (plastic, glass, metal, wood waste, electronic waste, construction waste),
2. use print or digital media to search for information on safe ways of handling waste materials,
3. discuss safe ways of handling waste materials (reduce, reuse, recycle, compost and burn),
4. practise safe disposal of waste materials (reduce, reuse, recycle, compost and burn),
5. visit the locality to observe handling of waste materials.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Handling Waste Materials together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Self-Efficacy: effective communication skills are developed as the learner discusses safe ways of disposing waste materials.

• Digital Literacy: learner develops interacting with technology skills when using digital devices to search for information on

safe ways of handling waste materials in the environment.

Values:
• Responsibility: learner engages in assigned roles when practicing safe disposal of waste materials.

• Patriotism: learner is conscious of belonging to the community as they visit the locality to observe handling of waste

materials.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Environmental Conservation: learner minimizes environmental pollution when reducing, reusing recycling waste materials.

Link to other Subjects

Agriculture: learner enhances skills on organic gardening when composting waste materials.
